decision: retain exact snapshot rollback while measuring bounded coordinator failure-path scaling through 5000 missions with both absolute and queue-normalized growth gates

reviews.correctness: Use the real MissionCoordinator failure path and preserve exact rollback invariants. Compare 1000-to-5000 growth both as wall-clock p95 ratio and normalized by the 5x queue-size increase so per-mission regressions cannot hide under a loose absolute ratio.
reviews.robustness: Require both 1000- and 5000-mission measurements for growth evaluation and fail closed if either is missing. Keep ghost-state, ownership leakage, and fail-closed poisoning assertions alongside scaling checks.
reviews.latency_resources_regression: Report p95 microseconds per mission, raw growth ratio, and normalized growth. Default normalized headroom is 1.2x over linear scaling, while the raw 6x cap remains as a coarse absolute guard. Avoid mutation-delta complexity until measured failure-path evidence misses these gates.

alternatives.rejected: larger correctness and regression surface without evidence that exact snapshot rollback is the limiting bottleneck

alternatives.approach: use only the raw 1000-to-5000 p95 ratio
alternatives.rejected: a 6x raw cap over a 5x queue increase permits roughly 20 percent per-mission regression without making that allowance explicit
poor CI predictability and unnecessary CPU/memory consumption

qa: Measure failed enqueue and failed claim at 10/100/1000/5000 missions, record p50/p95/max and p95 microseconds per mission, and fail if either the raw 1000-to-5000 p95 growth ratio exceeds 6x or queue-normalized growth exceeds 1.2x.
lesson: Scaling gates should express both total-cost growth and per-unit growth. Optimize rollback representation only when the same seeded failure path demonstrates materially worse-than-linear scaling or misses an explicit target budget.
